title: Access-shadowing in identity proxy causes cross-tenant RBAC bleed and audit gaps
creator: Maya Chen
description: Several enterprise customers operating Private clusters reported that users were intermittently granted elevated privileges after KMS envelope rotations and identity-proxy restarts. In parallel we observed missing audit entries for some cross-tenant operations. This ticket tracks triage, an urgent patch, and the rollout plan. The bug is reproducible on clusters using SAML/SSO with group-to-role mapping and identity-proxy caching enabled. We believe a race between cache invalidation, role-binding refresh, and KMS unwrap led to transient principal mismatch that allowed 'access-shadowing' where one tenant's group bindings were applied to another tenant's session context.
reproduction_steps: 1) Configure two tenants (A and B) in a Private control plane with SAML group->role mappings.
2) Enable identity-proxy with group membership caching (TTL 15s) and periodic KMS envelope rotation (every 60s).
3) Initiate SAML login for a user in tenant A and perform a privileged action (create model endpoint). Verify audit event written.
4) Trigger KMS envelope rotation and concurrently restart identity-proxy and inject a quick tenant binding refresh for tenant B.

5) Reproduce: perform privileged action as tenant A user while cache state is in-between refresh and KMS unwrap. Observe privileged action accepted and audit event showing tenant B context or missing required tenant id.
6) Same sequence is reliably produced in local minikube cluster when simulating network delay between control-plane and KMS and using small cache TTLs.

mitigation_actions: 1) Immediate mitigation: disabled identity-proxy group cache reuse across tenant boundaries and set cache TTL to 0 for affected clusters.
2) Enforced pre-apply tenant id validation at the RBAC layer (deny if token tenant != session tenant).
3) Temporarily paused automated KMS envelope rotations for impacted Private regions to reduce windows for race reproduction.
4) Proactive customer notifications sent with mitigation steps and guidance to rotate any questionable service credentials (Support lead email template attached).
fix_summary: Root cause: identity-proxy's cache key omitted the current KMS envelope version and tenant fingerprint under a particular race, allowing stale membership mappings to be applied to a newly-unwrapped principal. During KMS envelope rotation the unwrapped principalID could collide with an entry in the cache that belonged to a different tenant due to a shared non-unique cache key under heavy concurrency.

Permanent fix: include KMS-envelope-version + tenant-id in cache keys; add an explicit tenant-binding guard in RBAC evaluation; make unwrap-to-principal transitions linearizable with a per-principal mutex for the short window around unwrap + bind + cache-insert.
Additional: improve audit plumbing to flush pending audit events when unwrap fails and add end-to-end trace IDs for every auth flow that can be correlated to KMS rotation events.
deploy_plan: 1) Merge hotfix branch after Security sign-off (PR: GH-priv/hotfix/ENG-425999).
2) Deploy to staging with KMS rotation simulation and identity-proxy restart test harness (run smoke & regression suites).
3) Canary rollout to 3 Private clusters (low-traffic customers) with 1-hour observation windows and tight SLO alarms on audit counts and RBAC rejects/accepts.
4) If canary stable for 6 hours, expand to 25% clusters. Monitor metrics: tenant-mismatch-rate, audit-missing-rate, auth-latency, and KMS unwrap errors.
5) Full rollout targeted within 48 hours pending no regressions. Emergency rollback plan: if regressions occur, revert identity-proxy to previous version and re-enable paused KMS rotations.
qa_checks: Unit tests: new cache key invariants and per-principal mutex behavior covered (expected coverage +8 tests).
Integration: simulate concurrent unwraps with varied KMS latencies and assert tenant isolation preserved in 1000-run randomized tests.
E2E: run customer-sim clusters with real SAML IdP testbeds; validate audit sequence integrity and ensure no tenant id flips for privileged actions.
Performance: benchmark identity-proxy 95th p99 latency with new mutex in place; ensure <10ms added median for auth path under normal load.
postmortem_actions: 1) Schedule full blameless postmortem and publish within 14 days — include timeline, RCA, and customer impact matrix.
2) Add automated KMS rotation chaos tests into CI (simulate envelope rotation and assert no auth path impact).
3) Extend audit retention and create alert that raises on sudden drop in audit events for any tenant during KMS operations.
4) Product: review default identity-proxy cache TTL and offer safer default for new Private clusters (TTL=0 until explicit opt-in).
5) Security: run an inventory of keys and recommend key rolling for customers with potential exposure; coordinate support outreach.
